name: Miras / It's All Connected (Behrouz, Razaviyayn, Zhong, Mirrokni)
ontology_notes: Design framework for sequence-model associative memory. Four choices. Associative memory architecture, attentional bias (inner key-value objective), retention gate, memory learning algorithm. Instantiations are Moneta (L_p bias, L_q retention), Yaad (Huber bias, Titans-style L2 retention), Memora (L2 bias, KL retention via softmax). Unifies Transformers, Titans, and linear RNNs. Not a companion store. No user, character, relationship, lore, or OOC types.

ontology.evidence: Paper §4 and Figure 1. Memory is a parametric map from keys to values. Table 1 places Titans, Mamba, DeltaNet, and the three new variants on the same four axes. Axes are architecture knobs, not companion memory kinds.
ontology.label: measured

write_policy.evidence: Write is one optimizer step on the attentional-bias loss (paper §3-§5). Moneta uses ∇ℓ_p. Yaad switches L2 vs L1 by residual size δ_t. Memora writes through softmax(α log W - η ∇ℓ_2). No user pin. No joke filter.
write_policy.label: measured

read_policy.evidence: Read is associative recall from the memory module, optionally hybridized with sliding-window attention (Figure 2, §5.4). No retrieve-nothing social gate.
read_policy.label: measured

supersession.evidence: Retention regularizer balances new concepts against keeping W close to W_{t-1} (Learning-Retaining viewpoint, paper §3). Overwrite is a weight state, not invalidate-with-time on facts.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: Sequence index and chunked parallel training (§5.4). No calendar validity.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: One sequence backbone. No user vs character vs relationship.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: Evals are LM, commonsense, NIAH, recall-intensive. No skip-relevant-hit control.
silence.label: measured

poisoning.evidence: Yaad Huber loss is robustness to extreme tokens, not trust tags or jailbreak filters (paper §5.3).
poisoning.label: measured

forgetting.evidence: Paper Remark 3. Forget gates are reframed as retention regularization. The brain does not erase, retrieval fails. New gates include L_q and KL. Not a user forget-that command. Steal this framing.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: Chunked matmul training like Titans (§5.4). Memora uses linear updates inside a chunk and nonlinear softmax/log across chunks. 340M / 760M / 1.3B scales in Table 2. Hybrid -H variants add SWA cost.
cost_shape.label: measured

local.evidence: Paper HTML has no official GitHub. CC BY 4.0 on the PDF. No software LICENSE observed.
local.label: measured

mcp.evidence: Architecture paper. No MCP in https://arxiv.org/html/2504.13173.
mcp.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: Unifying theory for test-time memorization in sequence models. Moneta, Yaad, Memora are backbones, not companion APIs. Steal retention-as-regularization. Evals are LM, commonsense, NIAH. Those are not companion holes.

published_eval.name: Language modeling and commonsense (WikiText, LAMBADA, PIQA, HellaSwag, WinoGrande, ARC, SIQA, BoolQ), RULER S-NIAH, recall-intensive tasks
published_eval.claimed_score: 340M Moneta Wiki PPL 26.19. 760M Yaad Wiki 20.99. Hybrid Yaad-H Wiki 18.59 (Table 2). Authors claim variants beat Transformer++ and modern linear RNNs on LM, commonsense, and recall.
published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: Next-token perplexity, commonsense accuracy, and needle retrieval. Not companion identity, silence, poisoning, or forget-that.

open_unknowns: Whether official Miras/Moneta/Yaad/Memora code will be released.
